_authority: L25 - the person reading this does not work in IT. Read by scripts/check_plain_language.py. Edit this file, not the script.
_the_law: EVERY MESSAGE THAT LEAVES THIS FACTORY IS READ BY A MARITIME PROFESSIONAL WITH NO IT BACKGROUND. If it names a problem, it must also say where the thing is, how to open it, what to change, and how they will know it worked.
_why: The owner said it plainly: this person does not know the IT world at all. A report that says 'FAIL: check_visual_first.py - module.html:412 missing lead figure' is not a report to them; it is a wall. They cannot act on it, so they either ignore it or come and ask, and both of those are the factory failing to finish its own job. A finding nobody can act on is the same as a finding nobody made.
_this_is_not_dumbing_down: The maritime content stays exactly as technical as it is - cargo tank types, flammable limits, the IGC Code. What changes is the language about COMPUTERS AND THIS TOOL. A chief officer knows what an inert gas generator is and does not know what a stylesheet is, and nothing about the first fact excuses the second word.

every_problem_message_has_five_parts._rule: All five. A message missing any one of them sends the reader to find somebody who can read it.

parts.name: WHAT IS WRONG
parts.how: One sentence, in the words of the course, not the words of the software. 'Slide 12 explains the cargo pump but has no picture of one.'

parts.name: WHERE IT IS
parts.how: The FULL path, exactly as it appears on their computer, and the human landmark beside it: which module, which slide number, which heading. 'C:\Users\...\Module_04\module.html - slide 12, the one headed "The cargo pump".'

parts.name: HOW TO SEE IT
parts.how: The literal steps to open it and look. Double-click, which program opens, what they will see on screen. Never assume they know how to open an HTML file, run a command, or use a terminal.

parts.name: WHAT TO DO
parts.how: The actual fix, in steps. If the factory can do it, offer to do it and say so: 'tell me to fix it and I will'. If a person must decide, say exactly what the decision is and what each option means.

parts.name: HOW THEY KNOW IT WORKED
parts.how: What they should see afterwards. 'Slide 12 now opens with the pump drawing at the top.' Never end on 'run the check again' as the only proof.

never_say_without_explaining._rule: These words are fine ONCE the sentence has said what they mean in ordinary words. Used bare, they are the wall. The plain form goes first; the technical word, if it is needed at all, goes in brackets after it.
never_say_without_explaining._example_good: the file that controls how the slides look (its stylesheet)
never_say_without_explaining._example_bad: a CSS drift in the token layer

a_problem_with_no_way_out._what: The third check: a paragraph that names something wrong and never says what happens next. The reader is left holding it.
a_problem_with_no_way_out._why_the_lists_are_here: Both vocabularies started inside the script and both were too narrow. The next-step list missed 'find a real photograph' and 'somebody needs to finish them', so the checker complained about text that was already perfectly actionable - the cry-wolf failure this factory has a law about. They live here so widening them is an edit, not a code change.

how_to_write_a_path._rule: A person cannot act on a path they cannot find. Give the whole thing, from the drive letter, and say what to do with it.
how_to_write_a_path.good: C:\Users\raiviss\Desktop\gas basic\course\Module 04\module.html  -  copy that line, paste it into the address bar of a File Explorer window and press Enter; the folder opens with the file inside.
how_to_write_a_path._also: Say which program opens it. A slide file opens in a web browser by double-clicking. A settings file opens in Notepad by right-click, Open with, Notepad.

how_to_write_a_command._rule: Most operators should never be given a command at all - offer to run it instead. When one is genuinely needed, it is one line, complete, copy-pasteable, with the steps to reach the window it goes in and what a good result looks like.
how_to_write_a_command._prefer: Say: 'tell me to run the check and I will, and I will tell you what it found.'
if_you_must: one command, on its own line, nothing to fill in
how to open the window it is typed into, in clicks
what a good result looks like, in words - not 'exit code 0'
what to do if it says something else: come back and paste the whole message

tone._rule: Write to a competent professional in an unfamiliar subject, not to a beginner and not to a colleague in IT.
do: say what happened and what it means for the course
give the decision, not the diagnosis, when a person has to choose
offer to do the work: most fixes belong to the factory, not to them
keep the maritime vocabulary exactly as precise as it already is
do_not: apologise, hedge, or explain the internals of the tool
print raw tool output as if it were a report
leave the reader with a problem and no next step

surfaces._what: Where this law is enforced. Anything a person other than the factory reads.
surfaces._not: Code comments, test names and the scripts' own internal docstrings are written for whoever maintains the factory, and stay technical.
